newsitem.title: USA: Wildfires sweep through southern California.
newsitem.headline: Wildfires sweep through southern California.

text.p: Wind-whipped flames destroyed at least 12 expensive homes and damaged eight others in an exclusive Orange County community on Monday while firefighters battled a 1,500-acre (607-hectare) wildfire northwest of Los Angeles.
California's notorious Santa Ana winds, gusting up to 50 mph (80 kph), spread both blazes quickly, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate their homes.
The Orange County blaze in a posh suburb near Tustin was brought under control in about three hours, but not before it had wreaked havoc in the neighbourhood of million-dollar homes.

Residents of the Los Angeles suburb of Calabasas fled as fire raced through tinder-dry brush, fanned by the hot, gusting winds. Four schools were evacuated as the blaze spread at an alarming rate, with the dense smoke virtually blocking out the sun in some areas.
The brushfire brought back memories of the Malibu fires of 1993, in which hundreds of homes, including those of Hollywood movie stars, were burned to the ground.

The Santa Monica Mountains separate the San Fernando Valley, where Calabasas lies, from Malibu on the Pacific coast. Officials said the fire was racing through rugged terrain and had already swept through 1,500 acres. It was now headed for Malibu, famous as the home of the stars.

The Santa Ana winds, which spring up every October and often last for several weeks, were responsible for spreading the flames in the southern California firestorms of the fall of 1993, which destroyed nearly 1,000 homes and caused hundreds of millions of dollars in damages.

Orange County officials said the blaze near the town of Tustin, about 30 miles (50 km) southeast of Los Angeles, appeared to have started in a tree near a home. The house burned and embers from the fire carried by the wind spread to other nearby homes.
Evacuation of the area, including two nearby schools, was ordered by the fire department as flames soared 500 feet (150 meters) into the air, but no injuries were reported.
The Santa Ana winds also caused havoc with power supplies in Orange County, downing lines and leaving about 50,000 people without electricity at one point.

Both fires were fought on the ground and from the air, but high winds were also hampering the efforts of water-dropping helicopters, turning the water into a fine spray that had little effect on the flames.

So-called "super-scooper" planes, which scoop up thousands of gallons of water at a time and then deposit them on the flames, were grounded for a while in the Calabasas fire because of high winds and dense smoke.

In northern California, firefighters were close to containing a wildfire that had threatened homes and businesses along a scenic stretch of California's coast in the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty. It has consumed 668 acres (270 hectares).

Firefighters said cooler temperatures and a drop in the winds had given them the upper hand over the blaze, which broke out on Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.
